---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Gross-Claim Backed Cash Discount
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(che, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), lct), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Cash-to-market cheapness should be most predictive when gross profit can cover current liabilities.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Prior evidence favored cash-backed value when the quality leg addressed operating strength or claim pressure. This version avoids current-asset mechanical overlap and asks whether the apparent cash cushion is supported by recurring gross economics strong enough to satisfy near-term claims.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: After-Distribution Total-Claim Cash Value
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(che, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(oancf, dvc), lt), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Cash-rich firms should outperform when operating cash flow after dividends remains strong relative to total liabilities.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: A high cash-to-market ratio can still be a value trap if ongoing distributions and creditor claims absorb internally generated cash. This signal favors cheap cash balances only when the firm continues to generate residual cash flow after shareholder payouts, reducing the risk that cash is merely a temporary buffer.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Rollover-Safe Cashflow Yield
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(oancf, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(lct, lt), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: High operating-cash-flow yield is more valuable when liabilities are less concentrated in short-term claims.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Cheap cash flow can be illusory when near-term refinancing pressure prevents cash flow from accruing to equity holders. Conditioning cash-flow yield on a lower current-liability share targets firms where operating cash generation is less likely to be captured by urgent creditors.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Debt-Funded Payout Trap
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(dvc, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(GROWTH(lt, 1), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: High dividend yield should predict weaker returns when the firm’s liabilities are growing.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: A high payout yield is attractive only if it is sustainable from internal resources. When payouts coincide with rising liabilities, the dividend may be debt-funded or maintained despite deteriorating fundamentals, making the apparent value yield a potential trap.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Liquid-Cushion Earnings Yield
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ni, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), lt), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: High net-income yield should be more predictive when the firm has a liquid current-asset cushion relative to liabilities.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Earnings yield alone can select firms whose profits are threatened by liquidity stress. Requiring net current assets to cover a meaningful portion of liabilities helps separate cheap profitable firms from firms where creditor pressure may impair the equity claim.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: Claim-Quality Enterprise Multiple
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ebitda, ADD(ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), dltt), SUB(dlc, che))), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), lct), NEG(RATIO(lct, revt)))))
HYPOTHESIS: High EBITDA-to-enterprise-value firms should outperform when gross profit covers current claims and current liabilities are not excessive relative to revenue.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Enterprise-value cheapness can reflect operating mispricing or creditor overhang. This interaction keeps the valuation multiple distinct while using claim-quality measures to identify firms whose EBITDA is less likely to be consumed by short-term obligations.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Improving-Operations Cash Discount
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(che, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_ZSCORE(SUMRANK(TREND(RATIO(oancf, revt), 3), NEG(TREND(RATIO(cogs, revt), 3)))))
HYPOTHESIS: Cash-to-market cheapness should be more predictive when operating cash conversion is improving and cost intensity is falling.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite
REASONING: This avoids reusing the archived gross-profit-over-current-liabilities leg and instead tests whether cash-rich value firms are becoming operationally healthier. A cash hoard is more likely to be underpriced when the core business is improving, while cash-rich firms with worsening conversion or cost pressure may be cheap because the cash will be consumed.

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Nonexpanding-Claims Cash Value
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(che, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_ZSCORE(NEG(WINSOR(GROWTH(lt, 1), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: Cash-to-market cheapness should be strongest when total creditor claims are not expanding.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: This replaces the archived post-dividend cash-flow coverage recombination with a direct claim-dilution mechanism. High cash balances are more valuable to equity when liabilities are stable or shrinking, whereas cash-rich firms simultaneously growing liabilities may be using cash as a temporary buffer against deteriorating solvency.

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Maintenance-Covered Earnings Yield
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ni, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(oancf, dp), lt), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: High net-income yield should be more reliable when operating cash flow after a depreciation proxy covers total liabilities.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite
REASONING: This moves away from the net-current-asset cushion that produced contradictory evidence and instead tests whether cheap reported earnings have cash support after maintenance burden. Cheap earnings are more likely to be quality value when cash generation remains meaningful relative to creditor claims, rather than when profits are accounting-heavy or balance-sheet constrained.

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Asset-Wear-Safe Enterprise Value
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ebitda, ADD(ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), dltt), SUB(dlc, che))), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(NEG(WINSOR(ACCEL(RATIO(dp, revt)), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: High EBITDA-to-enterprise-value firms should outperform when depreciation intensity is not accelerating.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite
REASONING: This avoids stacking redundant current-liability coverage legs and focuses on a different enterprise-value trap: rising asset-wear pressure. EBITDA cheapness is more credible when depreciation burden is not accelerating relative to revenue, because the operating yield is less likely to be overstated by underrecognized maintenance needs.
